analysis: The supplied units are base-text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 2816-3290) from the BASE revision. The PR changes only documentation: it renames the v0.10.8 candidate heading to v0.10.9 and adds roughly 390 lines of release notes at the top of the file. The changed ranges are lines 11-400 on the head side. The supplied base excerpts are historical release notes outside the changed range, so they show no changed security behavior. I examined them against the threat model, including T-041 (cache), TB-011 (App Attest), TB-012, T-053 and the pair/solo lifecycle notes, and found no executable code, configuration, workflow or permission changes. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full head text of the new notes was not visible. Those notes describe pair/solo serving lifecycle fixes in provider updater and start/stop behavior. They may touch TB-003 and A-018 availability, but no source changes were supplied to evaluate. Remaining integration question: if later batches include provider-swift source for the pair serving, updater or stop --solo paths, they should be checked against the lifecycle ownership, the single-lock behavior and the release-gate assumptions. No finding is made from changelog prose alone.
